mainTopic: Whether the two כתובה clauses came from one בית דין, and when writing all one's property to someone makes them an owner or only an אפוטרופוס
overview: The amud has two topics. First, the גמרא asks how we know that two clauses of the כתובה, the sons' clause and the daughters' clause, were made by one בית דין. It tries to prove this from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who learns the daughters' rule from the sons' rule, since one תקנה can only be learned from another if one court made both. The גמרא rejects the proof: a later court could have matched an earlier court's wording on purpose. Then a new topic begins with שמואל's rule: a man who writes all his property to his wife has only made her an אפוטרופוס (manager), not the owner. The same holds for an adult son, and even for a baby son in his crib. If an outsider is named along with the son or wife, the outsider gets a real gift. A betrothed or divorced wife also gets a real gift. Finally the גמרא asks about a daughter alongside sons, and a wife alongside brothers or alongside the husband's sons. רבינא and רב עוירא give two different reports of רבא's answer.

steps.title: How do we know both clauses came from one court?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that the sons' clause and the daughters' clause were made by a single בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know they were made by one court? Maybe they were made by two courts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions an assumption it has been relying on: that the two כתובה clauses come from one בית דין. If they came from two different courts, there is no reason to read them as one connected statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the sons' clause in light of the daughters' clause only works if they belong together. If two different courts made them at different times, each clause stands alone. This challenge threatens the whole earlier reading.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this? A request for the basis of an assumption.
A court (בית דין).
They were made as rabbinic rules (instituted).
Perhaps, maybe.

phrases.english: From where do you know that they were instituted by one court?
phrases.notes: "They" means the two כתובה clauses, the one for the sons and the one for the daughters.

phrases.english: Perhaps they were instituted by two courts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier assumption, made before this section, that the two כתובה clauses are one unit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the sons' clause and the daughters' clause were made by one בית דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two separate courts made them, they are not one statement, so one cannot be read in light of the other.

steps.title: Proof from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's teaching in יבנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the two-courts idea by quoting a משנה where רבי אלעזר בן עזריה compares the daughters' rule to the sons' rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, because the earlier part of the משנה teaches: This teaching was taught by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה before the Sages in the vineyard in יבנה. The sons inherit and the daughters are fed. Just as the sons inherit only after their father dies, so too the daughters are fed only after their father dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by bringing a משנה from מסכת כתובות. There, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns a rule about daughters straight from the rule about sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה places the two rules side by side: sons inherit only after the father's death, so daughters are fed from the estate only after his death too. He treats the two תקנות as linked. The next step explains why this proves they came from one court.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't let that idea enter your mind. A firm rejection.
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא.
He taught an interpretation.
"The vineyard in יבנה", the name used for the gathering of חכמים at יבנה.
They will be fed and supported.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the daughters' clause gives a living father any duty to feed his daughters. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's point is that this support comes from the estate only after the father dies, just like the sons' inheritance.

phrases.english: This should not enter your mind,
because the earlier clause teaches:
phrases.notes: This comes from an earlier משנה in the same chapter, כתובות 49a.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה מִדְרָשׁ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: This interpretation was taught by Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
before the Sages in the vineyard in Yavneh:
The sons inherit and the daughters are sustained;
phrases.notes: These are the two כתובה clauses: sons inherit their mother's כתובה money, and daughters are fed from the estate.

phrases.english: just as the sons do not inherit
except after their father's death,
so too, the daughters are not sustained
except after their father's death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by bringing a source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a source showing the two clauses are treated as linked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two clauses may have been made by two unrelated courts.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns one clause from the other, which shows they belong together.

steps.title: Learning one rule from another needs one court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof: we can only learn one תקנה from another if the same בית דין made both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say one court made them; that is why we learn one rule from the other. But if you say two courts made them, how could we learn one rule from the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why the quote from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה proves its point. Learning one תקנה from another only makes sense if one court made both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One court is expected to set up its rules consistently, so its rules can explain each other. Two different courts have no such connection. Since רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does learn one תקנה from the other, the two must have come from one court.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say... A formula that sets up the 'good' option before the problem.
We learn or derive.
A rabbinic rule set up by a court.
How?

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּחַד בֵּי דִינָא אִיתְּקוּן,
phrases.english: Granted, if you say they were instituted by one court,
this is why we derive one ordinance from the other ordinance.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּתְרֵי בֵּי דִינָא אִיתְּקוּן,
phrases.english: But if you say they were instituted by two courts,
how can we derive one ordinance from the other ordinance?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּחַד בֵּי דִינָא אִיתְּקוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quote in step 2 proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: That the sons' clause and the daughters' clause were made by one בית דין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's teaching in יבנה, which learns one תקנה from the other.

steps.title: A second court could have copied the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: two courts could have made the rules, with the later court matching the earlier one so the rules would not clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe I can really tell you that two courts made them, and the later court made its rule to match the earlier court, so that one rule would not contradict the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 3. Two courts could still have made these rules, if the later court shaped its rule to match the earlier one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's comparison only shows that the two rules match. It does not show who made them. A later court may have copied the earlier court's pattern on purpose, so his comparison works either way. That means the proof for one court falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you... A way of holding on to the option that was just rejected.
Later, the second one.
Earlier, the first one.
It will contradict or clash.

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does not prove the two כתובה clauses came from one court. A later court may have matched an earlier court's wording, so the clauses may not be one connected statement after all.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the two clauses may come from two courts, the earlier attempt to read the sons' clause in light of the daughters' clause loses its basis.

phrases.english: From where do you know this? Perhaps I can actually say to you
they were instituted by two courts;

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵי דִינָא בָּתְרָא תַּקּוּן כְּבֵי דִינָא קַמָּא,
phrases.english: and the later court instituted its rule like the earlier court,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא תִּקְשֵׁה תַּקַּנְתָּא אַתַּקַּנְתָּא.
phrases.english: so that one ordinance would not contradict the other ordinance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in steps 2-3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that one court made both clauses.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Matching rules do not require one court, because a later court can copy an earlier court's pattern.

steps.title: Writing all property to one's wife makes her only a manager
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: if a man writes all his property to his wife, he has only made her an אפוטרופוס, not the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A man who writes all his property to his wife has only made her a manager (אפוטרופוס) over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from שמואל: writing everything to your wife does not give her ownership. It only puts her in charge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We assume he did not mean to cut his children out of their inheritance entirely. The language 'all my property to my wife' is read as making her the one in charge, so the heirs will respect her. The property still belongs to the heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: One who writes (a document giving property)
All his property
A manager or caretaker who runs property but does not own it

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the base for the rest of the passage. Every case that follows is measured against it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One who writes all his property to his wife –
has only made her a steward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the earlier discussion about which בית דין made which תקנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Writing all of one's property to one's wife makes her only an אפוטרופוס, not the owner.

steps.title: An adult son is obviously a manager, but what about a young son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that an adult son who receives everything is only an אפוטרופוס, and asks what the law is for a young son.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that if he writes everything to his adult son, he has only made him a manager. But what if he writes it to his young son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא extends שמואל's rule to sons. The adult son is easy, so it asks about the case that is not clear: a young son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An adult son can actually run the estate for his brothers, so calling him a manager makes sense. A young child cannot manage anything. So maybe the father really meant to give him the property as a gift. That is the doubt behind the question.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
His adult (grown-up) son
His young (minor) son
What (is the law)?

phrases.english: It is obvious: his adult son –
phrases.notes: The words 'if he wrote everything to' are left out here but understood, just like in שמואל's ruling.

phrases.english: he has only made him a steward.
His minor son, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 5's rule to sons and points out the case that is still unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does writing everything to a young son also make him only an אפוטרופוס, or does he get it as a gift?

steps.title: Even a baby in his crib is only a manager
steps.stepSummary: רב חנילאי בר אידי quotes שמואל: even a young son lying in his crib is only made an אפוטרופוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רב חנילאי בר אידי said in the name of שמואל: Even if it is his young son who is still lying in a crib, he is only a manager.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a quote from שמואל. Even a baby does not get the property as a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אפילו ('even') shows this is the hardest case, and the rule still holds. The child cannot manage now, but the father wants him to be the respected one in charge when he grows up. So a young son is treated just like an adult son.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Lying in a crib, meaning a baby

steps.whatToRemember: Writing everything to a wife, an adult son, or even a baby son makes them only an אפוטרופוס, not the owner.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, רַב חֲנִילַאי בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Ḥanilai bar Idi said that Shmuel said:
Even his minor son who is lying in the crib.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב חֲנִילַאי בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even a baby son is only an אפוטרופוס. The father's writing is not a gift to him.

steps.title: Family member plus an outsider: the outsider gets a gift, the family member manages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states it is obvious that if the document names his son or his wife together with an outsider, the outsider gets a real gift and the son or wife is only an אפוטרופוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if he wrote to his son and another person, the other person gets his share as a gift, and the son is a manager. If he wrote to his wife and another person, the other person gets his share as a gift, and the wife is a manager.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists cases it treats as obvious, where a family member and an outsider are named together. These easy cases set up the truly unclear cases the גמרא asks about in Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An outsider has no inheritance rights, so the only way to read his part is as a real gift. The son or wife keeps the same 'manager' status we already learned. Putting the two names side by side does not change how we read each one.

keyTerms.meaning: Another person, an outsider who is not an heir
A gift (real ownership)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the outsider is also just a manager. He truly owns his share. Only the son or wife is the manager.

phrases.english: It is obvious: his son and another –
phrases.notes: The case is a document that gives all the property to both of them together.

phrases.english: the other gets it as a gift, and his son is a steward.
His wife and another –
to the other as a gift, and his wife is a steward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'manager' rule from steps 5–7 and applies it to documents that also name an outsider.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a family member and an outsider are named together, the outsider receives a real gift and the son or wife is only an אפוטרופוס.

steps.title: A betrothed or divorced wife gets a real gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues its list of obvious cases. If a man writes all his property to his ארוסה (betrothed wife) or to his גרושה (divorced wife), she receives it as a real gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: His betrothed wife or his divorced wife: she receives it as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more obvious cases to its list. A betrothed wife or a divorced wife who is written everything really owns it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases, the son or wife was only made an אפוטרופוס. Here the result is the opposite: the betrothed wife and the divorced wife are not part of his household in the usual way. So the writing is read as a true מתנה (gift).

keyTerms.meaning: His betrothed wife: the קידושין has been done, but the full marriage has not yet taken place.
His divorced wife, his former wife.
As a gift. She truly owns the property.

phrases.english: His betrothed wife or his divorced wife
phrases.notes: This continues the 'it is obvious' list from Step 8. He wrote all his property to one of these women.

phrases.english: receives it as a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues Step 8's list of obvious cases, but here the result is the opposite: a real gift, not an אפוטרופוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A betrothed wife or a divorced wife who is written all the property acquires it as a real gift.

steps.title: Question about a daughter or wife when other heirs are present
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask about three cases where the man wrote everything to one person even though other natural heirs exist: a daughter when there are sons, a wife when there are his brothers, and a wife when there are his sons from another wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: a daughter alongside sons, a wife alongside the brothers, and a wife alongside the husband's sons. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real open question. In these three cases, is the person written everything a true owner, or only an אפוטרופוס?
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases fall in between the ones already settled. A son or wife was only an אפוטרופוס. A betrothed or divorced wife got a real gift. Here someone else would normally inherit, so it is unclear which way to read his intention.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים. This marks a real open question.
Alongside, when there also are. For example, a daughter written everything while sons exist.
The husband's sons, meaning his sons from another wife, not hers.
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: 'אצל' does not mean the property is shared. It means he wrote everything to the daughter or the wife even though sons or brothers exist who would normally inherit.

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
a daughter alongside the sons,
phrases.notes: He wrote everything to his daughter even though he has sons, who are the normal heirs.

phrases.english: and a wife alongside the brothers,
phrases.notes: He has no children, so his brothers would inherit, but he wrote everything to his wife.

phrases.english: and a wife alongside the husband's sons — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the obvious cases in Steps 8 and 9, the גמרא moves on to cases that are truly unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In these three cases, does the person written everything become the owner, or only an אפוטרופוס?

steps.title: רבינא's version: no ownership in any of these cases
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes רבא: in all these cases the person does not acquire the property and is only an אפוטרופוס. The only exceptions are the betrothed wife and the divorced wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said in the name of רבא: in all of them, the person did not acquire, except for his betrothed wife and his divorced wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer to the question. Following רבינא's report of רבא, the daughter and both wives are only managers, not owners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the general rule of שמואל from Step 5 covers almost everything. Writing all one's property makes the person an אפוטרופוס. Only the betrothed wife and the divorced wife, already listed in Step 9, are different.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of. He is reporting a teaching of someone else.
In all of them, meaning all the cases just asked about.
Did not acquire. The person does not become the owner.
Except for.

phrases.english: Ravina said in the name of Rava:
in all of them, the recipient did not acquire,
phrases.notes: So the person is only an אפוטרופוס, like in שמואל's rule from Step 5.

phrases.english: except for his betrothed wife and his divorced wife.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A daughter alongside sons, a wife alongside brothers, and a wife alongside the husband's sons are all only an אפוטרופוס. Only a betrothed or divorced wife acquires.

steps.title: רב עוירא's version: ownership except for a wife facing brothers or the husband's sons
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא quotes רבא the opposite way. In all these cases the person acquires, except for a wife alongside the brothers and a wife alongside the husband's sons, who are only an אפוטרופוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא said in the name of רבא: in all of them, the person acquires, except for a wife alongside the brothers and a wife alongside the husband's sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, opposite report of what רבא said. In this version, the daughter alongside sons truly owns the property, but the two wife cases do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real difference between the two versions is the daughter alongside sons. רבינא says she is only a manager, while רב עוירא says she owns it. Both agree that a wife alongside brothers or alongside the husband's sons is only an אפוטרופוס, and that the betrothed and divorced wives get a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquires. The person becomes the true owner.

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions of רבא agree on the betrothed or divorced wife (a real gift). They also agree on a wife alongside brothers or the husband's sons (only an אפוטרופוס). They disagree only about a daughter alongside sons.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not רבא changing his mind. Two different students report what רבא said, and their reports do not match.

phrases.english: Rav Avira said in the name of Rava:
in all of them, the recipient acquires,
except for a wife alongside the brothers
and a wife alongside the husband's sons.
phrases.notes: In these two cases she is only an אפוטרופוס. So the case left over that she owns is the daughter alongside sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of רבא's answer from the one in Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person acquires in all cases (including a daughter alongside sons), except for a wife alongside brothers or alongside the husband's sons, who is only an אפוטרופוס.
